facts.text: On this day in 1307, France's King Philip IV arrested every Knight Templar simultaneously — a coordinated dawn raid across an entire country, centuries before telegraphs or phones.
On this day in 1943, Italy declared war on Germany, its former Axis ally, switching sides just six weeks after Mussolini's fall.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Bangkok than outside it — roughly half of humanity within a single radius.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, containing about 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth, packing over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any borough of New York or Tokyo district.
On this day in 1987, markets were five trading days from Black Monday. The Dow would shed 22.6% on Oct 19 — the largest single-day percentage crash in U.S. history, dwarfing even 1929.
On this day in 2008, the Dow surged 936 points, its biggest single-day point gain at the time — a desperate relief rally mid-collapse, as governments worldwide pledged coordinated bank bailouts.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 by 24 brokers. The tree itself blew down in a storm. The exchange survived.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2 trillion valuation in 2019, making it worth more than Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet combined at the time.
The Dutch tulip mania of 1637 peaked with a single Semper Augustus bulb fetching 10,000 guilders — roughly the price of a Amsterdam canal house, for a flower.
On this date in 1999, scientists confirmed that the universe's expansion is accelerating — meaning most galaxies are already receding faster than light and will one day vanish from our sky forever.

On October 13, 1307, the Knights Templar were arrested en masse. Their suppression helped birth modern banking: their credit note system survived them and quietly became the foundation of international finance.

Your skeleton is not the rigid cage it feels like. Bone is a living tissue that completely replaces itself every decade, and it responds to stress by growing denser — it is, in a real sense, a muscle you never flex.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.

Mantis shrimp see with 16 types of color receptors — humans have 3 — yet research shows they are worse at distinguishing similar hues. They process color locally in the eye, bypassing the brain entirely.

On this day in 1307, Philip IV of France arrested every Knight Templar simultaneously at dawn — a coordinated operation so vast it wouldn't be matched in logistical scale until modern policing existed.
Oxford University was already 150 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates the empire Cortés destroyed.
On this day in 1943, Italy declared war on Germany — its ally just 47 days earlier. The same generals who signed the Axis Pact signed the new declaration.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was separated from Khufu by 2,500 years, from Apollo 11 by 2,000.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, before the American Civil War. Alexander Bain's 'electric printing telegraph' predates the telephone by 33 years.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast linguists debate whether invented words can go feral.
On this day in 1884, Greenwich was adopted as universal meridian — giving English the word 'deadline' its first real rival: 'standard time,' imposed on every clock from London outward.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable because English lacks the concept — homesickness fused with grief for something irretrievably lost.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of a used bookshop. Also coined by Koenig; that two invented words now feel ancient proves languages adopt what they need, not what they plan.
Snollygoster (n.): a shrewd, unprincipled politician. American English, attested 1846. President Truman used it in a 1952 speech, forcing journalists to look it up before they could file their copy.

On this date in 2023, the SEC's lawsuit against Binance expanded to name CEO Changpeng Zhao personally — he later pleaded guilty to AML violations and became the first CEO of a major crypto exchange sentenced to federal prison.

On this date in 2021, Coinbase's Q3 earnings revealed it held more ETH on its balance sheet than BTC — quietly signaling institutional preference for yield-bearing assets over the original store-of-value narrative.

Bitcoin's timelock opcode OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, activated in 2015, lets coins be mathematically locked until a future block height — the script itself enforces the embargo, with no custodian or counterparty involved.

The Ethereum genesis block, mined July 30 2015, contains the hidden message 'dao-hard-fork' embedded by developers — a timestamp proving the fork decision preceded the actual DAO exploit by nearly a year in planning culture.
Satoshi's original whitepaper never uses the word 'blockchain' — the term appears nowhere in the nine-page document, which instead refers to 'a chain of blocks' and 'the longest proof-of-work chain.'
On this date in 2016, DeepMind published 'WaveNet', a generative audio model that cut the gap between machine and human speech quality in half—measured by mean opinion score—overnight.

On this date in 2011, IBM's Watson had already beaten Jeopardy champions Jennings and Rutter eight months earlier, yet ran on a 2,880-core cluster consuming 80kW—a room of hardware to do what a phone now does.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have processed roughly 13 trillion tokens—if you read one token per second without sleeping, it would take 413,000 years.

The transformer architecture, now the backbone of nearly every frontier AI system, was proposed in a 2017 paper titled 'Attention Is All You Need' by authors who have since scattered across at least six competing AI labs.

Chinchilla scaling laws, published by DeepMind in 2022, showed that most large language models released before that year were simultaneously overtrained on compute and undertrained on data—a finding that invalidated years of prior scaling intuitions.
